clue.text: Turned white and pained after a lot of lost blood

indicators.note: a lot of a word, but not all of it, so the last letter of the synonym for lost blood is dropped

parts.note: to have lost blood is to have bled
pained means hurt, ached

explanation.surface: Someone went pale and felt ill after a heavy loss of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' signals that the synonym for lost blood loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hair or cloth that has been whitened with chemicals has been made pale.

clue.text: God heard supplication for support

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a plea for backing: back us!

explanation.surface: A deity listens to a prayer asking for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The plea 'back us' is said like the name of the Roman god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Roman god of wine and revelry.

clue.text: He goes in heart of USA heading off to their A&E

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: the American spelling of centre, a heart or core
ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital's A&E department

explanation.surface: A man walks into an American hospital's emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the C of CENTER; A&E is the British name for a hospital casualty department, ER in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal noun: one who walks into a place is an entrant.

clue.text: Fabricated swindle with last month put back and this one included

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so the current month goes into the reversed one
put back means turned round, so the letters of the month are reversed

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's last month
this month, the month of publication, October, abbreviated Oct

explanation.surface: A faked scam involving a clock-change of the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last month' is December, not the month before; 'this one' is October, when the puzzle ran. 'put back' makes CED, and OCT is 'included'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: made up, invented, as a story or excuse can be.

clue.text: It's a condition of old people; seeing where to source one wild fruit and another

definitions.text: It's a condition of old people

parts.words: where to source one wild fruit
parts.note: elders are the trees that bear elderberries
another wild fruit: the hip of the wild rose

explanation.surface: Old age, and foraging for hedgerow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'elders' as senior people of a community.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: the state of being one of the senior members of a church or tribe.

clue.text: Shot dead protecting heartless traitor — it's all over

indicators.note: something all over is turned head over heels, so the built letters are read backwards
protecting means wrapping round, so the word for dead goes outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes all the inner letters of traitor, leaving its first and last

explanation.surface: A traitor's death in a shooting, and that's the end of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's all over' (turned head over heels) reverses the whole container once built. 'Shot' is a past-tense verb, darted, not a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have shot across a room is to have moved very fast, to have darted.

clue.text: Further Away win

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for away in football results
to gain is to win

explanation.surface: A football fan hopes for another away victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: furthermore, besides, in addition.

clue.text: For Rattle, great musical work included — probably the Fifth

indicators.note: included means placed inside the jumbled letters
to rattle something is to shake it about, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: Conductor Simon Rattle's choice of a great symphony, likely Beethoven's Fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous conductor, so 'the Fifth' suggests a symphony; it is a car's fifth gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in a five-speed car the fifth gear is usually the highest one.

clue.text: Royal bonkers used such when partly out of uniform

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the letters are mixed
partly out of means only part of what is there is removed: one of the two letters for uniform goes

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A mad royal wore such things when half out of uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: USED SUCH has two Us; only one goes, hence 'partly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wife of a duke, a title in the British royal family.

clue.text: Where to work out the boundaries in geometry maths

indicators.note: the boundaries are the edges, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Where to solve problems at the edges of geometry and maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like solving sums but means exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: fitness centres where people exercise.

clue.text: What hairdresser might do is decided in advance

definitions.meaning: a stylist trims the hair and then blow-dries it
an idiom for a matter already settled, with no argument left

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a cut-and-dried result was settled beforehand, like pre-cut timber ready to use; the other reading is a salon's trim and blow-dry.

clue.text: Game might be set in this? Like a shot

definitions.text: Game might be set in this?

parts.note: like means as, in comparisons
a shot is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A cook's question about a game pie, then a quick comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is meat such as pheasant or venison, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: savoury jelly in which cold meats such as game are set and served.

clue.text: A length of time to hang around rowdy bar in refuge

indicators.note: to hang around something is to surround it, so the time word goes outside

parts.note: sixty minutes, an hour

indicators.note: rowdy suggests disorder, so the letters of bar are jumbled

explanation.surface: Spending an hour loitering near a noisy pub as a place of shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is anagram fodder for 'rowdy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sheltered port is a refuge for ships, and the word also means a safe haven.

clue.text: Honest following scriptural instruction

parts.note: since means after, following on from
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Someone truthful because they obey the Bible's teachings.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone genuine and truthful in what they say and feel.

clue.text: Sweden outside right gets hold of the ball and scores

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: outside means the next word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a fielder who takes hold of the ball catches it

explanation.surface: A Swedish outside-right winger takes the ball and nets goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside right' looks like a football position; 'outside' puts CATCHES round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scores as a verb means marks with lines, scrapes a surface.

clue.text: Building impacted mostly on pasture after the initial step

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: impacted means struck, hit

indicators.note: after the initial means what follows the opening portion, so the first part is cut away

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet

explanation.surface: A building collided with grazing land after the first stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step' is the ballet term pas, which opens 'pasture'; 'after the initial step' keeps what comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something constructed, an edifice or building.

clue.text: This man has got round the old taxman and employs workers

indicators.note: got round means surrounded, so the contraction for this man has goes outside

parts.note: he's, short for he has
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A man dodges the tax inspector and takes on staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got round' looks like evasion but signals a container. The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax office until 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a firm that takes on staff for pay engages, recruits, and employs them.

clue.text: A top-level cover-up — does it follow mad March days say?

indicators.note: say means as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.words: does it follow mad March days
parts.note: after the March madness of hares comes calm: hare peace

explanation.surface: A wig, and whether calm follows the madness of March.
explanation.walkthrough: Hares are said to go 'mad in March'; the peace afterwards would be 'hare peace'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: a wig or toupee covers the top of the head.

clue.text: Style of construction as advertised on radio?

indicators.note: on the radio a word is heard, not seen, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: advertised means billed, announced on a poster

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a building style is being promoted in a radio commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the make or physique of something, how it is put together.

clue.text: Most daring underwear

definitions.meaning: the most courageous, bold and fearless
a bra and a vest, both worn under clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word for courageous; read as two words it names two undergarments.

clue.text: I see polar bear's offspring perhaps caught inside a frozen block

indicators.note: caught inside means held within, so the young animal goes into the letter name

parts.note: see is how the letter C is pronounced, its name spelt cee
a young bear is a cub; 'perhaps' because any bear has cubs

explanation.surface: Spotting a polar bear cub trapped in a block of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' reads as an exclamation, but it is I followed by CEE, the name of the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a small frozen cube of water used to chill drinks.

clue.text: Roughly peels second bit of orange skin (left over) for zest

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely arranged, so the letters are mixed up
over here means finished, gone, so the letter for left is taken away
second bit of picks the second letter of orange

explanation.surface: Peeling an orange carelessly and keeping the rind aside for its zest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest' looks like citrus rind but means liveliness. PEELS, R and SKIN lose L ('left over'), and 'Roughly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: zest is lively enthusiasm, a bouncy cheerful energy.

clue.text: Seeing only Mr Bean's 'oddities', therefore all round restraint required

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so the word for therefore goes outside

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

indicators.note: oddities are the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Seeing just Mr Bean's quirks, a ban on such things is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is a British TV comedy character played by Rowan Atkinson; 'oddities' takes his name's odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official ban on trade, a restriction.

clue.text: How pointy bit of church rises?

definitions.text: How pointy bit of church rises?

parts.words: How pointy bit of church rises?
parts.note: the spire of a church is a steeple; in a sharp ascent, the adverb jokingly built from it

explanation.definitionFit: Adverb: rising sharply, at a sharp angle, as a church spire does.

clue.text: One more 25; he helps you in trouble

definitions.note: someone who assists another, especially in wrongdoing

parts.note: one means a, the indefinite article
25 across means competent; more competent is better

explanation.surface: One more able person comes to your aid when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to 25 across, CAPABLE, so 'more 25' is 'more capable': BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: an accomplice who assists or encourages someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Those things leading to end of mice? (as seen in this crossword)

parts.note: them, those things

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of mice

explanation.surface: Things that lead to the death of mice, as found in this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those things leading to end of mice' hints at the long-running play 27 across, the puzzle's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: the subject running through the puzzle, its unifying topic.

clue.text: The president's no leader, a butt

indicators.note: no leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Donald Trump, the US president

explanation.surface: The president is no leader, just a figure of ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a target of jokes but means backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the backside, the hindquarters.

clue.text: Competent dad put in some wiring

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the word for dad goes into the wiring word

parts.note: a cable is a length of wiring
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A skilled father installed a bit of electrical wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone able, skilled enough to do the job.

clue.text: Avoid opening of concert piece, giving piano runs a miss

indicators.note: giving something a miss means leaving it out, so the letters for piano and runs go
a miss is the second half of giving something a miss, leaving out

parts.note: a prelude is an opening piece of music
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Skipping the overture of a concert by not bothering with the piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving ... a miss' removes P and R from PRELUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dodge or evade, to escape from something.

clue.text: Opera must beat long-running play

indicators.note: beat as in battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera has to outdo a play with a long run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like 'outdo' but signals the rearrangement of OPERA MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Agatha Christie's murder mystery, running in London's West End since 1952.

clue.text: Research papers — the ones on hand surgery primarily

parts.note: these means the ones here, close at hand

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of surgery is taken

explanation.surface: Academic papers about operations on the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand surgery' reads as a medical topic; 'the ones on hand' is THESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dissertations written for a degree, papers presenting research.

clue.text: Formal act put Spain in credit with money all over the place

indicators.note: in places the Spain letter inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters of money are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting Spain in the black with cash spread everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is part of the container signal with 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ritual, a formal observance or occasion.
